title: Alexandre Kojève — The Cold Version #Shorts
description:
Take away the meaning and Alexandre Kojève still functions — that is the disturbing part. Alexandre Kojève (born Aleksandr Vladimirovich Kozhevnikov; 28 April 1902 – 4 June 1968) was a Russian-born French philosopher and international civil servant whose philosophical seminars influenced 20th-century French philosophy, particularly via his integration of Hegelian concepts into twentieth-century continental philosophy. Aleksandr Vladimirovich Kozhevnikov was born in the Russian Empire to a wealthy and influential family.

The self that experiences Alexandre Kojève is a committee, not a king. Drury, Shadia B. (1994), Alexandre Kojeve: The Roots of Postmodern Politics, New York: St. Violence and Conflict in Alexandre Kojève’s Works, Philosophical Journal of Conflict and Violence, Volume 8, Issue 1. 2024.
